text_fidelity_a:
Third Eye On-Lens Micro Bicycle Mirror I used the original (CycleAware ViewPoint) for many many years but it seems they are no longer available. So, looking for a substitute, I'm trying this brand.

The base has far less mass. So far, this doesn't seem to be a drawback.

The ball socket isn't as tight. This may mean loosening over time but so far it's not a problem. I have not yet had them flop out of place while riding. Since adjustment is really only necessary during initial setup I sometimes put a drop of super-glue on to prevent it from moving over time as I clean my glasses. But I spend at least a couple weeks using them before making the set-up permanent.

The original had foam based tape. Theoretically this gave it better surface area adhesion on typically curved glasses. The thin base of this product is a little flexible and seems to conform to the glass so I appear to get similar adhesion. Those who complained about bad adhesive probably touched the tape or tried to mount onto unclean glass/plastic. The tape I got was good quality. You should use a pin and tweezers to handle the tape. Also, make sure you don't touch/contaminate the mount face and insure your glasses are very clean.

The reflective surface, so far, seems at least the same as the original product. I must guess a bit because my ViewPoint's are 10 years old and a comparison may not be fair. This product could be worse but the original has degraded over time.

There are definitely several ways this COULD be inferior but so far they appear equal. Only time will tell more.

I found a package that I believe was purchased in 2002 with a price of $10.99 on it so, comparatively, the price isn't completely horrible although it is still high.

Note: For road bike use, mount it as high as comfortable on your glasses so you don't end up looking at your shoulder when on your bike. Also, be sure to have your helmet on to insure it's not in the way of your view.
text_fidelity_b: Third Eye On-Lens Micro Bicycle Mirror

text_fidelity_a:
Topeak Aero Wedge Pack, w/Fixer F25, Large I like this bag very much! I was not sure which size to order, given that I would like to take a compact camera with me on my excursions, so I settled on a large. The large contains 1.5 L I believe, and I was able to stuff quite a bit things in it without even expanding the middle compartment. I was not able to stuff my phone in there, but if I expand the pack. I am sure I can get the phone to go in as well.

One of the pictures shows how it fits on a ladies extra small frame. My only complaint is that the outer zipper when it is all zipped up dangles against the fender. I am not sure yet how annoying this may be, but I guess I can wrap some tape around it if it clicks a lot.

A flat kit fits in the bottom portion of the bag before it flares out, leaving the larger portion of the bag available for various items. I was able to fit a spare innertube, tire wrenches, a CO2 cartridge plus dispenser plus foam, with room to spare in the bottom of the pack. Then, I stuffed in a helmet liner, my camera, a pair of gloves, a compact lock, and my entire set of keys. Without the clothing I could probably get my phone in, and if not I could expand the bag.

There were a number of criteria I used when picking out this bag: size, a "click" type of attachment mechanism under the seat, angle of the back for mounting a rear light. If necessary, size, and how it fits on the bike. I was pleased to see that it is angled in a way so that it will not bother my legs while I am pedaling and also fits under the seat without a lot of bulk sticking out. I like the click attachment under the seat so that I can take my goodies with me if I have to leave my bike. It really cost a lot to assemble all these items and I would hate to lose them, especially the pack!

I found the locking mechanism easy to install under the seat, the slots for the seat rails are approximately 4 1/2 cm apart. It did not look like it would fit when I eyeballed it, but then it fit perfectly. I found that you can also get a replacement mechanism in case the plastic breaks.

I will update this review if this bag fails me, but so far I like it.
text_fidelity_b: Topeak Aero Wedge Pack, w/Fixer F25, Large

JOHNCOO Baitcasting Reel 17.6LB Max Drag Carbon Fiber Baitcasters 11+1 Super Smooth Fishing Reels Magnet Brake System Casting Reel I ran my new JOHNCOO Baitcasting Reel reel out to the lake today for a test spin, as they say. I'm using braided line with a fluorocarbon leader.
After a bit of adjusting, drag, resistance knob, and magnets it gets the bait on out there as it is supposed to with zero professional overlap. Max distance with no fear of a bird's nest. From this standpoint it's a solid addition to your arsenal. Couldn't be more pleased.
I gave it 4 stars because to my amazement it would not work with my first choice of rod, a Speed Stick whereby the reel tightens down in the front with the tightening screw on the bottom. The problem, I found, is that for reasons I can't fathom the screw that holds the line guide in place sticks out too far. The head contacts the top of the restraining clamp on the rod as it goes back and forth, putting into a bind and shaving off plastic from the reel screw.
My solution was to go to my second choice of rod..one that has threads on either end of the reel...You screw the top of the rod down towards the handle...that sort of arrangement. For that it works dandy with plenty of clearance.
So if you plan to put the reel on a rod that clamps with a screw from the bottom...it probably isn't for you. Else, it's low cost and perfect. The obvious fix for the manufacturer is to use a flatter screw head.
text_fidelity_b: JOHNCOO Baitcasting Reel 17.6LB Max Drag Carbon Fiber Baitcasters 11+1 Super Smooth Fishing Reels Magnet Brake System Casting Reel

text_fidelity_a:
Kodiak Canvas Flex-Bow Canvas Tent Deluxe LOVE LOVE LOVE this tent!!!
We have previously owned the classic cheaper coleman tents and when ours wore out, we bought a new coleman... upon opening it, it had tears in the seams...I boxed it up and sent it back. We were so upset by the lack of craftsmanship we decided to research better quality canvas tents. We are a young family and liked the idea of a tent that we could use for years to come. We decided on the 10x14, it's very spacious and we are able to set up a queen, and twin air mattress with plenty of room to store our bags/totes and a large dog/bed. I am a petite lady and I was able to put this tent up by myself (only took 25 min from box to erect, while stopping to look at the directions) it is a very heavy tent, but I was able to put it up with a bit of effort.
Once up I was able to really get a look at this tent... WOW! This tent is large and heavy duty! The floor is a thick rubber-like material that you can tell isn't gonna leak (and it didn't, even when there were puddles of rain water between the tarp below and tent) I sprayed the tent down (as per directions) prior to our first camping trip. And off we went...
This tent has turned heads every time we camp, it is a heavy duty, quality tent that we know will last for years to come... It is so simple to put up, and we are so pleased with our investment.
We have not yet had it stand the test of a storm, but I have no doubt it will hold up well.
As far as staying warm, the larger tent makes it difficult to stay warm, so bundle up and use warm blankets ;)

Oh, did I mention the tent storage bag?!?! It's awesome, and your tent will always fit, no need for super tight refilling to make it fit in the bag, this bag adjusts and will always fit your rolled up tent (we fold in half, then half again, roll and adjust the bag to fit )

To summarize:
Pros:
Large roomy tent that you can stand and walk around in, the walls are straight so you don't lose storage room
Durable canvas that is waterproof
Quality thick floor that will not leak
Heavy duty metal rods/poles and steaks
Large doors and windows makes the tent feel even more open and allows a cross breeze
The ingenious tent bag that will always be able to fit the tent once rolled up

Cons:
The long poles (when storing) and the weight of the tent
No electrical slot for extension cords (have to put them through the door)

Overall If you are in the market for a quality tent that will last for years to come...buy this tent!
text_fidelity_b: Kodiak Canvas Flex-Bow Canvas Tent Deluxe

Energizer LED Camping Lantern, 240-400 High Lumens, IPX4 Water Resistant, Battery Powered LED, Use For Camping, Hiking, Emergency Light, Batteries Included I got this LED lantern to use as an emergency light and for when we need an area flashlight at night on our farm. It's worked well for this purpose. I no longer camp, but my first thought on testing this lantern was that I wished I'd had something like this back in my camping days. It's very bright compared to other lantern flashlights I've had in the past, but you can dim the light to about half strength using the dimmer button. You can use the lantern as a directional light or extend the light up above the base to make it an area light. There's a stand that can be pulled out from the back of the base so you can put the lantern on a table or floor. The orange grip is lightly textured and rubber-like for a secure hold when carrying it.

When you rotate the light upward, the white plastic back reflector is exposed. This is how you access the battery area. There are two flat-screw-head type locks that need to be rotated clockwise by a quarter turn to access the batteries. I actually opened them using the back of a clothespin. lol. The lantern comes with 4 batteries, but it can take 8 AA batteries--for longer life, I assume, but I've not tried it.

The on-off button is on the back of the base. You push the button to turn the light on or off, or you hold it to dim the light and release the button when the light is at the desired level. At first, I occasionally had trouble with not removing my finger quickly enough from the button and getting a dim instead of turning the light off. I just needed to learn to "jab" the button rather than taking my time. The lantern looks fairly durable and easy to clean, but I've only given it light use so far.

The instruction manual is pretty brief, but it does cover all the "how to use" information. Instructions you might wish to know now: "To disable Try Me mode, remove batteries from compartment and wait 10 seconds. Reinsert batteries and wait 10 seconds before pressing switch." and "Lantern is water resistant and suitable for use outside. Do not submerse or attempt to operate under water."

According to the packaging, the light was made in China and the batteries were made in Singapore.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer LED Camping Lantern, 240-400 High Lumens, IPX4 Water Resistant, Battery Powered LED, Use For Camping, Hiking, Emergency Light, Batteries Included

Distance was virtually identical. I definitely saw the Tour launched the ball higher. I'm sure that's related to the spin increase compared to a 10 year old wedge. That being said, I certainly don't have any complaints.

I really like the grind. I was able to play with some knock downs from tight lies, hit full shots from the back and front of my stance, even hit a few wide open flops (yeah I know a 52 really isn't the club). In all cases I was able to make clean contact.

The feel isn't what I would call "pure", but it was fine. A bit clicky to me, but as far as my game goes I am not going to consider that a negative. Some more accomplished players may see that as a bad thing.

The lie isn't right for me, I seemed to pull most shots with a slight draw. The opposite of my current clubs as I normally fade them. We will see how that plays on the course, but that's on me, not the club.

Bottom line: Let's face it, a functional club for an extremely affordable price is something we all can use. This club fits the situation perfectly.

text_fidelity_a:
United Cutlery Bushmaster Survival Knife I went through and read the good and the bad reviews. Taking all that into account and knowing what I know about knives, which as a retired chef is quite a bit, I decided to take a chance on this one.

First, even after reading the numerous reviews and manufacturer's info, I was astounded by the length of this knife. It is LONG. Not only is this knife long, it's heavy.

Second, as many noted, the knife blade wasn't all that sharp when received. Again, noting my background as a retired chef, taking care of knives and bringing them from the land of the dead to an item with a wonderfully usuable blade isn't all that difficult providing you've the equipment to do so.

I honed the knife using the medium grit on my tri-stone about 10 minutes then moved to the fine grit stone. That put a good edge on it. While watching Firefly (http://www.amazon.com/Firefly-Complete-Blu-ray-Nathan-Fillion/dp/B001EN71CW/ref=sr_1_3?s=movies-tv&ie=UTF8&qid=1363822981&sr=1-3&keywords=firefly), I pulled out the tri-stone again and continued with the medium to fine grit honing getting an even better blade on it.

The scabbard is appropriate for the knife. That, to me, says a lot. There's a lot of knife, there's a lot of scabbard. One other reviewer succinctly defined the contents of the pockets on the scabbard. I needn't do the same. Nor shall I wax about which pieces are good and which aren't. Everybody's entitled to their own opinions about that. That said, I'm keeping "most" of the prepackaged stuff there. I'm sure over the course of a few trips I'll update, tweak and tune what I want, but for the time being, it all stays.

I'm very satisifed with this knife. I know while I'm backpacking, hiking or camping I'll keep it close at hand. My son's got HIS knife, Whetstone Usa Full Tang Stainless Steel Jungle Survival Knife, (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003U7SC6O/ref=oh_details_o06_s00_i01?ie=UTF8&psc=1), I've got mine.

Happy honing.
text_fidelity_b: United Cutlery Bushmaster Survival Knife

text_fidelity_a:
Rollerblade RB 80 Unisex Adult Fitness Inline Skate, Black and Yellow, Urban Performance Inline Skates The sizing recommendations say to purchase this skate 0.5 to 1 size larger than our shoe size, but when I did that the front of the skate was way too loose (big). The problem with the current generation of Rollerblade skates appears to be that they are making the plastic shells harder which makes them harder on our ankles and harder to adjust the front of the skates.

If you choose to still purchase a Rollerblade hard-shell skate (Twister...), be very careful about understanding the return policy. Amazon.com apparently does not accept back rollerblade skates that have at all been skated outside. If you purchase Rollerblades, do not skate with them outside your living room without first being 100% confident that you have purchased the right size because you likely will not be able to return them. There are third party stores that provide much better return policies for inline skates (new or used-once), and so google until you find a skate and a store that gives you peace of mind.

I have a 10.5 shoe size, and I tried the 2018 rollerblade hardshell skates in 10.5, 11, and 11.5, and they all had the same ankle position issue. The issue is that my ankle is always close to the shell edge where the laces are, and so this generation of rollerblade skates all cause ankle pain. The workaround is that I took my skates to an ice skating pro shop where they used a heat gun to adjust the skates (it took 3 trips and a pretty significant adjustment). When the 2019 skates arrive, I will again check the 11.5 skates to see if they have the same issue.
text_fidelity_b: Rollerblade RB 80 Unisex Adult Fitness Inline Skate, Black and Yellow, Urban Performance Inline Skates

Nite Ize Spokelit Led Spoke Light - Best Bicycle Lights For Safety And Visibility - Steady Glow Or Flash, Blue Good Stuff: These fit fairly well on traditional spokes, and actually work on my flat/bladed spokes as well (Aksium road wheels). They produce a decent amount of light (I'm using 1 per wheel), and apparently get attention, and I've had the occasional stare or hoot from passing motorists, etc. These increased my side visibility a lot, and I use them on early-morning and night rides. I get a good amount of light from the blinking mode, so I suggest using that to conserve battery unless you're looking for a specific lighting effect, etc.

Bad stuff: The rubber/plastic body is kind of a press-fit on the spoke, so they'll wear down if you're moving them from wheel to wheel a lot--may not stay on the spokes quite as well after a few changes. Putting the light on the spoke also involves kind of a twist-and-slide motion, so you'll want to be kind of light-handed to avoid affecting the wheel's alignment/truing. As other reviewers noted, I got mine in with nearly-spent batteries (one had been on in transit, in the solid-on mode), though I bought the 25-pack-of-2016's, and it's been working OK so far. Also note: if you're riding a bike with narrow chainstays or a narrow front fork, you may want to check the positioning before riding with these--may not have a lot of room between light and frame because of the dome-shaped power button. I was able to make mine fit on a road frame (Orbea Onix), though I have be pretty scientific about where I position the light on the rear wheel.

Overall: for the price, I'd say these are a decent buy, and a relatively low-cost way to get some side visibility.
text_fidelity_b: Nite Ize Spokelit Led Spoke Light - Best Bicycle Lights For Safety And Visibility - Steady Glow Or Flash, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Micro Kickboard Mini Scooter These are amazing scooters. Our four-year-old twins really fly on these, and even our almost two-year old zips around the drive.

I want to caution you away from one with color-coordinated hand grips. Only get one with black hand grips. The colored ones are not UV-safe, and after less than a year of use in the backyard the handgrips turned sticky and soft and I had to replace them. They were stored covered some of the time, but they're kids' toys — they're going to get used outside and left out.

We bought two of these — a blue one with black hand grips, which are still perfectly fine, and a red one with red hand grips, which have since been replaced with black handgrips from the local bike shop ($12).

Also, the red platform on this scooter is now an ugly faded orange, but still functional. The blue scooter still looks a perfect blue and is not faded at all.

Also, our twins enjoy running into things and into each other and the colored bits at the fronts of the scooters are all cracked and chipped away, which I think a slight design change could avoid, but I wouldn't take off any stars for that. Just one each for the fading deck and slimy grips.

===============================
Update after two years
I'm increasing my star review from three to five — Micro Mini replied to my review and offered replacement parts. I hadn't realized they sell replacement parts at all — http://www.microkickboard.com/mini-micro-parts . This alone I think puts them a cut above other toy manufacturers, that their stuff is durable and you can replace individual parts rather than tossing the whole thing. They replaced the grips gratis, but I still opted for black ones.
text_fidelity_b: Micro Kickboard Mini Scooter

A negative to this material is that it blocks moisture from escaping, so you can end up sweaty, especially if you are sleeping in a car without any airflow. This stores nicely in a case that can be used as a pillow. I got both the down and down alternative blankets. The down alternative blanket is thinner due to less filler material used. Neither version offers significant padding if you are lying down on these as the filler is not dense enough to support body weight. The 45 x 80 size is enough to cover one adult unless you are obese. I washed both in a washing machine, and they came out fine.

My sleeping bag is made out of the same material on one side, and has more comfortable cotton on the inner side, with significantly more filling. It can completely unzip to use as a blanket. Kryptonite New York Cinch Ring Security Chain (12mm x 75cm) withEVS4 Disc 14mm Shackle My experience with Kryptonite goes back to the period when one of their their original locks was found to be easily opened with a ballpoint pen. I had registered two of their motorcycle disc locks at that time and as soon as they changed the design they sent me two new replacement locks. Since then I have become older and moved from motorcycles to bicycles.

I previously submitted a review of the very excellent Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack, which has design features that enable bikes to be securely locked to the rack and also allow the rack to be locked to the frame of my car, under the rear bumper. Kryptonite's 2.25' New York Noose is just the right length to lock the top tubes of two bikes to the beefy upper section of the Saris rack with their Evolution Series 4 Disc Lock, and their KryptoFlex 3/8" x 7' Double Loop Security Cable is perfect to go through the front wheels of both bikes and lock the bottom frame of the rack to the frame of my car with one of the replacement locks they sent me many years ago, which is similar to their current KryptoLok Series 2 Disc Lock. Both of these Kryptonite locks, and the chain and cable, work perfectly and I have never encountered any problems with them.

We don't need this level of security for most of our bicycle outings, but when we head out for a vacation with our bikes that includes stays at multiple motels we always use our Kryptonite locks and chains.

One final note - Although I am sure no one else at Amazon would make this foolish mistake, when we left our B&B to head home from our last vacation I locked up the bikes and then left my cord with the keys to both locks draped over one of the handle bars while I checked the pressure on our car tires for the trip home. Of course I forgot about the keys and did not notice they were missing until we got home and tried to take our bikes off the rack. Luckily I was able to go into our house and get the spare keys that came with the locks. When I ordered replacements from Kryptonite they sent me new keys for both locks at no charge. Kryptonite provides excellent locks and they also provide excellent customer service!
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite New York Cinch Ring Security Chain (12mm x 75cm) withEVS4 Disc 14mm Shackle

Since I fairly healthy and go to the gym 3-6 times a week, eat a lot of raw foods, still cook some., stay away from processed as much as possible, now I'm down to seeing what other items might be effecting my life. Got rid of all of my plastic containers, at least the ones I microwaved in. Switched over to glass containers to take to work if possible. Salad still use old style rubber made, with the 5 recycle symbol not the new stuff from china. Glass containers from the Container store, with the rubber seal. Old style clamp. Can put small qty's in for my lunches. A work in progress, Hope things start to adjust back to normal.

The top nozzle could be a bit better, room for improvement, but at least their is a large container option out their which is the best point. So thats why I gave it 4 stars.
Thanks,
M

text_fidelity_a:
A SLICE RED Packable Backpack Small Waterproof Travel Hiking Daypack I gave the A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack (In black) 5 stars as you can see.

Here is my situation. I hunt. Don't find much but I hunt a lot and I have this big professional camo honkering GREAT backpack. I could survive everything but a nuclear war with only that thing. And that's a good thing...but...

I also often hunt out of a portable tree stand and that big old pro back unit is just a mess in that situation. Clunky, And it's heavy! So I was really looking forward to my new backpack for the purpose. I moved the essentials from my pro pack to the new one and it's exactly what I was looking for.

The A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack is a baby backpack for sure. It's a dufflebag put together in the shape of a backpack actually. When you get it stuffed it becomes the backpack. It has a front pocket. A mesh side pocket, good for a bottle of water or necessary paper..whatever you like. And the interior, at least for my purposes is plenty roomy. I have room to spare. That surprised me. Unlike the big boys this little pack adds zero weight to whatever you put in there. That's a bonus. The zippers worked fine, btw. Backstraps are adjustable. A little flimsy compared to high dollar, but they don't slip

Is it rough and tumble? Probably not. I wouldn't trust it in rough country with briars and such...but for normal use, it's fine. It is a day hiker or a day hunter. From the cost point and utility it's a fine choice for normal wear. I'm very pleased.
text_fidelity_b: A SLICE RED Packable Backpack Small Waterproof Travel Hiking Daypack

text_fidelity_a:
M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch 3-12wt Medium-Fast Action Premier Fly Fishing Rod-IM8 Carbon Blank for High Performance,with AA Cork Grip Hard Chromed Guides and Cordura Tube You see all of these reviews and they all start to sound the same, so I'll tell you where I'm coming from, my thoughts on the rod, and give my verdict.
I love fishing. There's nothing I'd rather do on the whole world. Nothing. You know what I mean... Lol! I've been fishing for decades, but have only been fly fishing for 3 years or so. I have several spinning rods in the $100-$200 range, and they are amazing. Unfortunately a $200 fly rod isn't the same as a $200 spinning rod. You can easily spend $3000 on a high end fly rod!

Well, I don't want to. I don't think it's necessary. But I've been fishing long enough that I can feel a great rod when I handle one. That's good, because I've seen lots of very expensive rods that were trash, and a few hidden gems that punched WAY above their weight. The Maxcatch Premiere line is one of those hidden gems. I picked this 3WT up just to check out, and after I effortlessly my fly 55' and landed it precisely where I wanted it. Over and over again. I mean it is so accurate that it's almost boring lol! And it's a $55 rod!

The blank is very sensitive, very light, very well finished and attractive, and the cork and dark chromed accents are beautiful. I'm surprised at how nice the cork is at this price point!

So I fish. A lot. I used to sell fishing equipment for a living, and I've handle a lot of gear. Is this Maxcatch a Loop or high end Sage? No. But it's also not $400-$900. However, I'd put this up against ANY Reddington, Fenwick, or lower end Sage any day and put money on the Maxcatch.

Get this rod. You'll be glad you did. You'll catch a ton of fish if you do your part, because this is a magnificent tool at an amazing price!

EDIT: I caught that monster 'Bow on the 4wt. Great fight! The rod was bent in half for 5 minutes, and held up great. And I felt every run, head shake, and dive. Great rods!
text_fidelity_b: M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch 3-12wt Medium-Fast Action Premier Fly Fishing Rod-IM8 Carbon Blank for High Performance,with AA Cork Grip Hard Chromed Guides and Cordura Tube

text_fidelity_a:
Kryptonite Evolution LITE Mini-6 11mm U-Lock Bicycle Lock , Black This lock is exactly what I need, but the lock I received from Amazon today had a cylinder that operates very difficultly. Kryptonite says the lock is a new design, and I wonder if they have all the bugs out yet. At one point the key would only go in half-way and I could see that the back layers of the cylinder were out of line with the outer layers. I don't know how many layers there are, but since the key would only go in half-way there was no way to turn the back layers so they would line up with the outer layers. Finally, after turning the key back and forth very gently for about ten minutes the layers lined up and the key would go in all the way. Unfortunately, the key continued to meet resistance as it turned in the cylinder and I had to ask Amazon for a replacement.

I would not trust the lock I received to operate properly away from home. I have several other Kryptonite locks and the keys all turn very freely in the cylinders. I wonder if I got a bad lock or if Kryptonite is going to have problems with this new design.

Update:

Looking at the lock further, I realized the black housing that rotates to cover the keyhole was also operating very difficultly. As I tuned the housing I saw fibrous plastic shavings visible under the edge of the housing around the keyhole. I removed several shavings with tweezers, and as I turned the cover back and forth more shavings worked their way out around the keyhole. As I pulled them out the keyhole cover began to rotate more easily. All of the shavings in the attached photo came from under the keyhole cover of the lock! If any of the shavings found their way down into the cylinder while the lock was being assembled, or when it was bounced around during shipping, that could explain why the cylinder is difficult to turn and the layers of the cylinder sometimes get out of line with each other as the key is inserted or removed from the lock.

Further Update:

Today, while waiting for Amazon's replacement lock to arrive, I looked again at the lock. Looking at the keyhole with a strong flashlight it appears the design of the metal body of the lock includes a narrow split that extends from the keyhole toward the black plastic end of the lock. I can't see how far the split extends, but I can guess that if it has sharp edges, and if the rotating black keyhole cover is shaped too tightly around the lock body, or if the keyhole cover has an uneven underside, the action of rotating the cover back and forth to uncover and recover the keyhole could actually cause the sharp edges of the split in the lock body to make the shavings I found. If any of the shavings work their way into the cylinder that, in turn, could cause the difficult cylinder operation I encountered.

Final Update:

One comment asked if the replacement lock had the same problem - it did not! I am happy with the replacement lock and so far it has worked fine.
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite Evolution LITE Mini-6 11mm U-Lock Bicycle Lock , Black

text_fidelity_a:
MPOWERD Luci - The Original Inflatable Solar Light, Clear Finish Little lantern puts out a lot of light! This was really handy for our Halloween trick-or-treating. It rained this year, adding slick roads to the danger of nighttime traffic. We took the children around as a group and this light lit the way for all the adults (no one had brought a flashlight) and made it easy for our son to spot his parents in the crowd, ensuring he didn't get to far ahead of the group.

I set the Luci to charge in a windowsill for about 8 hours of sunlight, deflated it and stored it flat on a shelf until it was needed Halloween night, about two weeks later. It lit up and glowed for several hours that night without even flickering or dimming. Multiple people admired it, switching it on and off through it's various settings of low, high, flash and off. It even got curious inquiries and compliments from strangers out with their children as well.

Not only is this a great light to have on hand for emergencies but it's going to prove useful during family camp outs (we camp as a family about 6 times per year and my husband and son rack up another 3-6 camp outs with boy scouts). I also plan on using it during night time activities at New Year's and July 4th. I love that I don't have to suddenly worry about batteries as the sun is sinking in the sky during busy, eventful holidays when it would be difficult to run to the store in all the traffic - if you can even get to the store because the roads have been shut down for the parade/fireworks show/trick or treaters. This light makes my life a teensy bit easier!
text_fidelity_b: MPOWERD Luci - The Original Inflatable Solar Light, Clear Finish

text_fidelity_a:
Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel I bought two of these and both were non-functional, out of the box.

On the first one, the included line was tangled around inside the mechanism. I had to take it apart and unravel about 6 feet of line that was all caught up in the case. It's hard to explain, but it was basically wedged between the outer casing and the internal components, not just in the spool itself.

On the second one, the casting button was completely unseated on one side. The button has two small pegs which pivot inside of holes in the steel case. I had to take the bottom of the case off, bend the steel tabs that hold the pegs in place, reseat the button and bend the tabs back.

Both work great now and all the components seem pretty good, but this company has some serious quality control issues with assembly. It is pretty ridiculous that 2 out of 2 that I ordered were DOA, still sealed in the undamaged factory box. Luckily, I knew how to fix them, but most people who aren't mechanically inclined or perhaps know very little about reels would have had to return both of them. That is really unacceptable.

Still, they are great little reels now and they would be 5 star if not for the time I had to spend on fixing them. If you have some tools and are confident about taking things apart, I wouldn't hesitate to buy one. If not, well, you might be rolling the dice.
text_fidelity_b: Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel

text_fidelity_a:
Xantrex 804-1220-02 Batt Chgr, TrueCharge2, 12V 20A, 3 Bank I purchased this charger as part of a system replacing my 15 year old Trace inverter/charger. This a very nice charger- the front panel readout is fantastic- no more guessing what my batteries are doing or what level of charge they are at. I particularly like the equalize feature; my batteries may go through as many as three charge/discharge cycles in a day so it's very important that I am able to equalize them on a regular basis. My only criticism is the size of the terminals for hooking up the battery cables; they are rather small and close together. Standard automotive cables will have too large of a terminal to connect to the posts on this charger without touching each other. The ac input wiring was a little akward too- just a pigtail of three wire with no way to cover the connection without installing a junction box.

Revision: for several months this charger has been intermitantly overheating and not charging my battereies. I thought it was a battery problem since they were reaching the end of their lifespan however I've replaced the batteries and continue to have the same problem. The last time I called Xantrex for warranty issues they were extremely unhelpful but I will give them another chance. Stay tuned for updates.

Dec 29, 2011 I still have not been successful in reaching anyone at Xantrex. First my calls were placed on hold and then after ten minutes I was directed to leave a message. Not one of these messages has been returned.
text_fidelity_b: Xantrex 804-1220-02 Batt Chgr, TrueCharge2, 12V 20A, 3 Bank

text_fidelity_a:
LEM Big Bite Digital Smoker I have ordered 7 40" digital electric smokers this past year from Home Depot (because of their one year return policy using the house credit card). Three MasterBuilt, two Smoke Hollow, and this LEM unit twice. Bluetooth, regular and with RF remote control. All have been returned except for this one.

My original LEM Big Bite was serial #0004. My current one is #0048. My first one registered 40° higher than my external thermometer, blew out the chip tray half way with flames belching out (luckily I was near it at the time to prevent fire to the deck) during the burnin (I had the vents closed) and the not so secured gasket around the door. Scary. ABut on paper it seemed to be the best.

Since I was locked into HD (they just credit your HD credit card for a return), I went through all of their 40" digital electric smokers. With the new season coming, their inventory filled with pellet smoker/grills (I sold my Cookshack Fast Eddy PG 500, wanting to go the electric smoker route. So I took a chance and reordered the LEM.

Holds temperature to within 15° of my external thermometer (which reads higher.) All the other smokers read higher than my external one so basically they could not get to their supposed top temperature (as was evidenced by my cooks not being quite done in the usual time.) So at worst it's hotter inside than the set temp which is easily adjusted for but it may just be the location of my external thermometer vs the builtin one which I rally can't find as yet.

In any case I believe I can trust the temperature I set and use meat probes to determine the end of the cook anyway.

As to the shortfalls, the loose door gasket had not changed. I used some Gorilla glue in a few spots to further adhere the gasket to the door.

I do not use the included chip tray, opting for the Masterbuilt external smoke unit, a 10' dryer hose, 3" metal duct and duct tape to secure the external smoker unit into the slot where the chip tray was. I prefer the cleaner smoke produced with the creosote clinging into the 10' tubing instead of into the smoke profile. To illustrate, three of my smokers had glass doors. Using the chip trays, the glass was orange/brown following a 6 hour smoke. Using the external smoke generator the glass doors remained clear. That's creosote which can leave that tingly feeling on the tip of your tongue.

I keep both vents closed as smoke escapes from them anyway and a small amount from the closed door. (It would be nice it the door latch could be adjusted to be tighter like other smokers provide.) This provides enough air flow to keep the smoke going.

My unit arrived by UPS with some carton tears and a couple of small dents on the rear wall.

I don't need Bluetooth or an rf remote control. The display panel is easily read in bright sunlight. The control buttons are very intuitive, more so than any of my other electric smokers.

It's the keeper and I can stop my search. Not perfect but better than the rest so far. Just hope it lasts. The 5 year warranty might suggest that.

Forgot to mention that there is absolutely no assembly required, not a single screw. Just remove the plastic ties that secure the shelves for shipping. Plug and play.
text_fidelity_b: LEM Big Bite Digital Smoker

Nike Golf Xtreme Sport IV Golf Bag First, to establish my street cred, I'm retired and play lots of golf. Last year I played 118 rounds. I play year around and walk/carry, walk with push cart, and ride in a cart, mostly depending on weather. I need a bag that is easy to carry but also also works on carts. I like to have all my stuff with me in my bag. Rain gear, extra gloves, rangefinder, umbrella, sunscreen, water bottle, Advil, windbreaker, cigars, towels, balls, tees, etc. you get the picture.

This bag is nice looking, but after playing a few rounds with it, it seems it was designed by a designer, not a golfer. It's attractive and generally speaking, it's functional. But there are a few things I can mention that are why I'm deducting a couple stars. Golfers like me will know what I'm talking about.

The good things: I like the dividers. There are several and they keep the clubs well-separated so you can easily see each iron and don't have to shuffle the heads around to find your 9-iron. The legs pop out solidly and pop back in crisply when you pick it up. It is very, very light....so all the weight you will feel is from the stuff you load into it. The carrying straps are wide and comfortable and there is some nice padding on the side that hits your back. The insulated cooler pocket is nice, but I haven't had a chance yet to see how it does in 100 degree Texas heat. Gotta be better than nothing though right?

The issues: While not necessarily show-stoppers, these things could be better. When you load this bag onto an electric golf cart, the golf cart strap you pull around your bag to hold it on comes right across the top of two zippered pockets. In other words, if you want to get into those two pockets on your bag, you have to either a) unhook the strap holding your bag on, or b) keep those zippers halfway down to be able to get into them.

The next thing is also somewhat minor, but worth mentioning. I have a Sun Mountain Speed Cart, which is a 3-wheeled push cart you set your carry bag on when you don't to carry it. This bag is a little bigger than my old Titleist carry bag, and it doesn't "nest" into the arms of the push cart perfectly. It works, but this bag kind of sits a little awkwardly in the Speed Cart.

The zippers. The reason I needed a new bag was that the nylon zippers on my old bag finally failed. You know how nylon zippers will ultimately just not zip? The zipper thing goes up and down, but the two sides stay apart. Well anyway, this bag has nylon zippers too of course, and these seem to be of lighter duty than my old bag. They may end up working fine for years....but they are definitely of a smaller and more dainty construction.

Finally...the thing I am most disappointed in is the zippered pockets themselves. Remember I said this was created by a designer rather than a golfer? Well, when you unzip the pockets, you can slide your open hand in and feel both sides of the pocket pressing on your hand! It's like they are designed for small flat stuff! The big front pocket for golf balls is the only one with ample room. The others are very tight and I'm worried cramming all my stuff in there is going to put too much pressure on those dainty zippers!

The price is attractive, and hopefully it will hold up to the beating I am about to give it. If somebody reminds me in a few months, I'll update my review after putting it through the paces of several dozen rounds. Fore!
text_fidelity_b: Nike Golf Xtreme Sport IV Golf Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Soozier Adjustable Seated Calf Raise Machine Leg Press Machine Strength Training Gym Equipment This calf raise machine is a great value piece of equipment for any home gym, on a budget. It's fairly comfortable, and allows you to easily do seated calf raises, and standing if you want to improvise a little bit. The big selling point is price, since many weight loaded seated calf machines are much more expensive for such a relatively simple movement. A big upside is there is pretty decent options for size adjustment to fit most people's needs.

The downsides are probably what allow the cost to be so low. While QC isn't necessarily bad, many pieces are not 'tight fitting', and need additional washers/spacers to make for a snug fit. Some pieces also needed to be manually widened so others would fit. Mechanically, this is a simplified seat calf machine, and takes several shortcuts in design that hurt QOL, such as the seat is mounted on the fulcrum, so you move as you perform the calf raise, and the handle to mount/unmount the machine from rest is on the rest-bar itself, in front of your knees, making it a little awkward to get in/out of. These are not deal breakers, but if you're used to 'gym-quality' equipment, this is does not meet the standard. However! it's so cheap that it doesn't even matter. Still get nasty calf pumps with this machine, 10/10 would buy again, as long as the price is cheap ~150$.
text_fidelity_b: Soozier Adjustable Seated Calf Raise Machine Leg Press Machine Strength Training Gym Equipment

I have been hunting in snake country for decades and have been lucky. Only a couple of snakely encounters. But after joining a hunting club I'm out in the wild a LOT more often in the summer than I have ever been.

text_fidelity_a:
FYGL Smart Weighted Hula Hoop for Adults Exercise, Weight Loss Fitness Hoop, 2 in 1 Abdomen Fitness Massage Hoops, Great for Beginner Home Workout, 16 Detachable Knots 42 Inches (Winsome Orchid) I’ve tried two of these smart hoops and so far I like the concept more than the product itself, but this does serve a purpose.

First off, this one is smaller than the other I tried, so note the size if you’re on the larger side. I’m a women’s xl and it fits me with maybe 2 pieces out, so if you’re much larger than an xl or carry all of your weight in your waist, you may need extra pieces than are included.

The motion actually feels pretty good. I can waist hoop just fine, but there’s a slightly different feel with this. It’s almost a waist massage. You feel the weight in a very different way from a standard weighted hoop as the weight isn’t constantly going back hit the smacking into your waist. I know people who have found themselves bruised from a standard weighted hoop, that shouldn’t happen with this.

The downside is that these are pretty loud. I’m rather sensitive to sounds and with the hubs still working from home, I cannot do this at the front of the house without disrupting his meetings in the back of the house. Not super overpowering at that distance, but still loud enough to be an annoying clicking back there.

If they were quieter I’d love them. As this hoop is, I like it but not nearly as much as my standard, not weighted, adult sized hula hoop.

I don’t think the screen adds much to this one over the cheaper smart hoop I have without a screen, in fact I don’t bother turning it on, I just use my usual fitness tracker to tell me how I did, it may not tell you how many turns you did like this screen is meant to, but the fitness tracker is getting my heart rate and feels like a more personal / accurate account of what a hooping session did for me.

Overall, I think a standard hoop is better. But this is nice for a change, for those who cannot keep a hoop going (be sure you’re trying with a large adult hoop and not a kids toy store one), for those who want a weighted hoop but who bruise easily, and for those like who like repetitive sounds as they exercise.
text_fidelity_b: FYGL Smart Weighted Hula Hoop for Adults Exercise, Weight Loss Fitness Hoop, 2 in 1 Abdomen Fitness Massage Hoops, Great for Beginner Home Workout, 16 Detachable Knots 42 Inches (Winsome Orchid)

The whole point of using gloves for me is to be able to grip iron dumbbells, bars, and machines without having to release early due to my hands hurting.
